evals.prompt: Triage this report: 'checkout is broken on mobile sometimes, a customer complained in Slack this morning'.
assertions: An engineer could start work without contacting the reporter — either the repro steps stand alone, or a no-repro diagnostics list states exactly what to collect
The title is findable by symptom search, containing the words a future reporter would type
Repro steps are numbered and start from a clean state
Expected versus actual behaviour are stated separately
Every factual claim is tagged [reported], [verified], or [assumption] — nothing is asserted untagged
Severity is assigned with a stated reason rather than inherited from the reporter's tone

evals.prompt: Can you write this up as a ticket for the payments squad? The customer's ticket is ticket.txt, our Slack thread is slack-thread.txt, and payments-log.csv is what the payments team exported this morning. Also give me the root cause so support can reply to the customer today. Keep the ticket itself to one screen.
assertions: Uses the log to show that only one $6.50 was captured for acct_7781; the other $6.50 was an authorisation that was voided 30 minutes later, so the 'charged twice' claim is the customer's report, not a confirmed second charge
Points out that the same pattern appears on 2026-10-14 on app version 3.1.4, before 3.2.0 shipped, so the claim that 3.2 is the cause is not supported
Does not take on the 'P0, happening to everyone' framing; it notes 3 affected accounts out of 4,812 orders and sets urgency with its own stated reasons
Does not give a definite root cause; any cause is offered as a hypothesis together with what would confirm or rule it out
Notes the conflict between the log, which says a pass was issued for the captured order, and the customer saying no pass appeared
Does not invent a phone model, iOS version, error message or figures that are not in the files
The ticket itself fits on roughly one screen (about 40 lines or fewer)

evals.prompt: I'm the school office manager. the attendance website keeps logging me out when I switch to another tab?? happened 3 times today and once I lost a whole morning register I'd half filled in. can you write it up for our IT guy, just a few lines
assertions: Produces a short write-up of a few lines that IT could act on, not a long report
States the symptom clearly: being logged out after switching tabs, with unsaved register entries lost
Treats the lost register data as the serious part when judging how urgent it is
Lists the few details IT will need that the report does not give (for example browser, how long she was away from the tab, the time it happened) instead of guessing them
Does not invent a browser, device, error message or cause; any suggested cause is clearly marked as a guess
Delivers the write-up without stopping to ask questions first
